rules: The cycle stage immediately following a reversal: after price has stopped going down, it coils into a wedge — often beneath the moving averages — and then “pops” out the top, reclaiming the averages and confirming a new up-cycle.
At the transition from down-cycle to up-cycle — after a Reversal Extension, as the change of character is confirmed.
Price tightens into a wedge (converging range, contracting volatility) after a reversal off lows, frequently still below the 9/20-EMA.
Break of the wedge’s upper trendline together with the reclaim of the 9/20-EMA; on earnings, the gap-up that pops the wedge with a strong close.
Below the wedge / consolidation low.
Trail the 9/20-EMA as the new trend develops; scale into strength on reward-to-risk.
